title: Decision: Production type compile-time check in tests
description: Why this is good: The _assert_production_state_compiles() test is a compile-time check that AppState<LocalApiClient> actually satisfies all trait bounds (WhoIsProvider, Send, Sync, 'static). This catches a class of bugs that would only appear at integration time: if LocalApiClient doesn't actually implement WhoIsProvider, or if it's \!Send due to hidden interior mutability, the code would fail to compile here. This is better than discovering the problem when wiring into main(). The function is never called at runtime (dead code annotation), but its presence in a test module ensures it's kept in sync with reality. This pattern is a solid alternative to running the production code in tests.
